newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on firm peso.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 75 basis points on Friday in the wake of the peso firming against the dollar, traders said.
"The market was not very liquid, nonetheless we could say that foreign dealers began to make themselves felt," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 3.6 pesos stronger at 7.8600/7.8630 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 80 basis points at 25.50 percent.
Some dealers felt that secondary rates had fallen due to speculation by players holding hefty positions.
"Apart from the fact that the forex market calmed down, some are hanging on to their paper," one dealer said.
Banco de Mexico injected 6.384 billion pesos into the market to offset liquidity shortfalls by auctioning a single three-day credit, which it assigned at 25.89 percent.
Liquidity shortfalls had originally been estimated at 7.464 billion pesos, due to credit maturities, but traders said investors stepping into the market also added liquidity to the market.
Total credit maturities for Monday were estimated at 6.398 billion pesos.
